My land is only 1.1 mu, so I cannot afford to waste anything, but I also cannot afford a bad harvest. Every year I do wheat then maize, same as everyone in our village.

For winter wheat, I will plant in early October after the maize comes off. I use improved seeds — I buy from the same dealer in town, the Jimai variety most people around here plant. Before sowing I spread one bag of compound fertilizer (15-15-15, 50 jin so 25 kg) as base — that gives me my phosphorus and potassium and some nitrogen. Then at the jointing stage in spring I topdress with urea, about 15 kg, because the wheat needs nitrogen to push up the stems. If the wheat looks yellow I add a little more. I plough the ground before sowing — my husband hires the tractor for half a day, costs about 50 yuan for our little plot.

Wheat needs water. I irrigate before winter (dong shui) so the roots survive the cold, then at jointing, and at grain filling — three times from the well. For pests I spray once for aphids in spring and once with a mixed spray for powdery mildew and aphids before heading. Two sprays is usually enough on such a small plot.

For summer maize I sow right after the wheat harvest in June — no-till, just push the seeds into the stubble, that is what everyone does now, saves time and money. I use a hybrid seed, Zhengdan or similar, the dealer recommends whatever is popular. At sowing I put down about 25 kg of compound fertilizer in the row. When the maize is about knee-high (big flare stage) I topdress urea, maybe 20 kg, that is the critical time. Maize needs less water than wheat — I irrigate once or twice if the rain does not come, especially at tasseling. One spray for corn borer is usually enough.

Last year my wheat gave about 450 kg and maize about 550 kg per mu. I expect similar this year if the weather is normal.
